text:
Jordan (sales): heads-up — acme corp demo just failed with a 413 when they uploaded their product bundle + metadata in the request body. they hit the demo path in the hosted api.
Maria (solutions): ugh, what size are they sending? full stack of images + large JSON metadata?
Jordan (sales): yes. payload ~6.8MB; base64 images + long product descriptions per item (hundreds of tokens each).
Sam (engineer): 413 from which component? gateway/nginx or our app? any logs?
Jordan (sales): getting `413 Request Entity Too Large` from the gateway in the curl response, customer saw `request rejected` in UI.
Priya (oncall): can you paste the curl they used (sanitized)?
Jordan (sales): paste below (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST \ 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_..." \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3-large","input": "<huge JSON with base64 images embedded>" }'
```
Maria (solutions): a few quick options: 1) presign + multipart upload for large blobs, 2) ship images separately and reference URLs in the prompt, 3) compress the payload (gzip) and set content-encoding if gateway supports it.
Sam (engineer): Agree. Also: for demo path we have a default body limit at the edge (nginx) configured ~5MB on hosted. We can raise it for this demo tenant temporarily but need ops approval.
Priya (oncall): I can bump to 10MB for a short window. need the tenant id and exact window.
Jordan (sales): tenant acme-demo-21, window tomorrow 2–4pm PT. can we do that?
Sam (engineer): +1 but prefer long-term fix: advise customer to presign images to S3 and include signed urls in the prompt. avoids big POST to the API and reduces cost.
Maria (solutions): customer worried about security — they want to keep data in their environment. options: 1) private deployment / dedicated capacity, 2) presign to their own S3 behind VPC, or 3) upload encrypted blobs to our presign endpoint (we can support).
Jordan (sales): they asked about a quick developer workaround we can put in the demo code.
Sam (engineer): simplest short-term snippet: chunk the prompt client-side and call streaming generation with incremental context. e.g., split descriptions, keep only top-K items in prompt, or reference embeddings for long context.
Maria (solutions): snippet for chunking we give in examples:
```
// pseudo
for chunk in split_items(items, 20):
  resp = client.generate({ model: 'rwd-3-large', input: prompt_with(chunk), stream: true })
  process_stream(resp)
```
Priya (oncall): If they need the whole context preserved for quality, recommend: 1) use embeddings store for large contexts, 2) retrieve most relevant passages at request time, 3) keep final prompt small. This reduces payload but preserves semantic recall.
Jordan (sales): pricing question from them: does presigning + separate storage change billing?
Maria (solutions): our hosted billing is per-token for generation + per-embedding when you call embeddings. Storage/transfers are on their side (S3). So presign approach doesn't change Redwood token billing beyond generation.
Sam (engineer): also note: model selection matters. some model variants have a higher max context (rwd-3-xlong vs rwd-3-large). if they need >8k tokens, propose xlong.
Jordan (sales): can we temporarily switch them to xlong for the demo?
Priya (oncall): yes, we can give a demo access key pointed at the xlong variant; need to record this in the rollout log.
DeployBot: scheduled config change queued: increase body_limit for tenant acme-demo-21 to 10MB — window 2026-03-22T14:00:00Z to 2026-03-22T16:00:00Z.
Jordan (sales): thanks. any final docs we can send the customer with the recommended approaches?
Maria (solutions): I'll send a 1-pager with: presign + S3 pattern, client-side chunking + streaming example, embedding retrieval flow, and note about model variants + when to request a temp body limit increase.
Sam (engineer): add a tiny code snippet for `Content-Encoding: gzip` + `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` too — some customers can gzip client-side and it bypasses base64 bloat.
Jordan (sales): perfect. I'll share the 1-pager and request the tenant window. :thumbsup:
Priya (oncall): I'll approve the nginx bump for the window once I see the tenant id in the ticket.
Maria (solutions): copying the customer-facing checklist into the ticket now.
Jordan (sales): ping me once the DeployBot change is confirmed and I'll run the demo.
DeployBot: change applied; nginx body_limit increased for acme-demo-21. will revert at end of window.
Jordan (sales): confirmed — demo completed successfully, customer happy. closing loop. :tada:
